basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 38.' and it opens 'Vers. 38. Minor quoque peperit filium, et vocavit nomen ejus Amon. Amon filius populi'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 38. Minor quoque peperit filium, et vocavit nomen ejus Amon. Amon filius populi mei, vel filius generis mei interpretatur. Isti fructus sunt ebrietatis, Moabitae et Amonitae, id est, qui ex patre sunt diabolo, juxta quod Dominus talibus dicit: Vos ex patre diabolo estis (Joan. VIII, 44). Et sunt filii populi invidentis et persequentis sanctos.
